quizSrc.term: The evolution of hotel chains between 1920 and 1950 was driven by: A. The emergence of loyalty programs B. A reduction in operating costs C. Declining travel costs D. the development of the air, road and rail network
quizSrc.definition: D. the development of the air, road and rail network

quizSrc.term: What are the four key players in the hotel industry value chain? A. Operators B. Employees C. Brands D. Distributors E. Consultants F. Owners G. Private equity funds
quizSrc.definition: A. Operators C. Brands D. Distributors F. Owners

quizSrc.term: In order to be able to scale quickly, hotel chains use franchising and management services contracts A. True B. False
Typically the initial cost of a franchising is a mixture of a flat fee plus a certain amount per roomA. TrueB. False
A management services agreement typically includes clauses related to:A. BrandingB. DistributionC. Hotel OperationsD. All of the above
All regions of the world remain dominated by independent hotels with the exception of AsiaA. FalseB. True
If a hotel actual occupancy rate is 45 % when it's theoretical occupancy rate is 20 %, it's Market Penetration Index is:A. 2.25B. 120C. 225
RevPAR is calculated byA. Dividing total room revenue by the number of rooms availableB. Dividing total room revenue by the number of room sold
quizSrc.definition: A. Dividing total room revenue by the number of rooms available

quizSrc.term: Hotels with index numbers above 100 are considered as outperforming their competitorsA. TrueB. False

Which of these descriptions best describes revenue management?A. The art and science of trying to maximize RevPAR using the elasticity of the demandB. Offering the right service, at the right time, at the right price, to the right customer, and through the right channel, in order to maximize RevPAR at the lowest cost of distribution.
quizSrc.definition: B. Offering the right service, at the right time, at the right price, to the right customer, and through the right channel, in order to maximize RevPAR at the lowest cost of distribution.

quizSrc.term: Before the electronic revolution, reservations typically came:A. Directly to the propertyB. Through tour operatorsC. Through corporate travel agenciesD. All of the above
To make use of GDSs, hotels needed to have:A. contracts with the major tour operatorsB. access to a Central Reservation SystemC. an existing relationship with corporate travel agents
quizSrc.definition: B. access to a Central Reservation System

quizSrc.term: As a result of the growth of the web, the number of potential pathways between the hotel and the consumer exploded... A. ...increasing both the complexity and potential of electronic distribution. B. ...but independant hotels successfuly resist this trend by limiting the number of channels with which they work. C. ... making it easier for hotels to manage their distribution.
quizSrc.definition: A. ...increasing both the complexity and potential of electronic distribution.

quizSrc.term: One of the major benefits of working with OTAs is wider distributionA. TrueB. False
Today, working with OTA's, the most widely used business model is:A. The commission modelB. The merchant model
For most hotels, working with OTA's has replaced traditional channelsA. FalseB. True
Bookings that come from a hotel website are less expensive than bookings through an OTAA. TrueB. FalseC. It depends

What is price parity?A. A clause in the OTA's supplier contracts that prohibits the latter from offering a cheaper price for the same product on any other distribution channelB. A critical piece of merchandising that helps convince the customer to stop searching and actually make their purchase.
quizSrc.definition: A. A clause in the OTA's supplier contracts that prohibits the latter from offering a cheaper price for the same product on any other distribution channel

quizSrc.term: To calculate the true cost of a brand.com booking, which costs do you need to consider?A. Website developmentB. Transaction cost (booking engine, credit card fees)C. Content maintenance costsD. Online marketing costs
quizSrc.definition: A. Website development  B. Transaction cost (booking engine, credit card fees)  C. Content maintenance costs  D. Online marketing costs

quizSrc.term: Disruption in terms of hotel distribution is likely to come from:A. AmazonB. GoogleC. MicrosoftD. Facebook
The meta search business model typically works... A. ...on a cost per click basis B. ... on a cost per acquisition C. ...on a commision per booking basis
quizSrc.definition: A. ...on a cost per click basis

quizSrc.term: Why is a hotel website content important?A. Competitors will mock you if your website doesn't look good.B. It plays a determining role in both being found by search and converting the webite visitor.C. Drive business to a website with poor descriptive text and low quality images would be counterproductive.
quizSrc.definition: B. It plays a determining role in both being found by search and converting the webite visitor.

quizSrc.term: To understand how to improve both your site and your sales, you should pay particular attention to:A. Insights from your analyticsB. Your hosting strategyC. The topicality of your content
When registering a domain name, you should also consider:A. Registering common mispellings of your nameB. Its similarity with your competitor's domain name
quizSrc.definition: A. Registering common mispellings of your name

quizSrc.term: For hotel websites, images and videos are important in convincing the customer to buy...A ...in all casesB ... for economy and budget hotelsC ...when moving towards the upmarket and luxury end of the market
quizSrc.definition: ...when moving towards the upmarket and luxury end of the market

quizSrc.term: According to Google, when trying to find an airline seat, customers search for:A. the brand name of the airlineB. a low cost carrierC. cheap flights
Using a database-driven approach to web development gives a more dynamic result, but is expensive and requires more sophisticated hosting options.A. TrueB. False
Using a virtual server provides flexibility and frees the website developer from maintenance requirementsA TrueB False
Using a pay for position strategy is attractive because it's performance oriented - you pay for what you get.A. TrueB. False
To decrease the cost of using display advertising, you need to focus onA. Decreasing CPMB. Increasing CPMC. Increasing CTRD. Decreasing CTR
quizSrc.definition: A. Decreasing CPM   C. Increasing CTR

quizSrc.term: When using affiliate marketing, you typically reward partners for every website visitor delivered?A. TrueB. False
When sending promotional emails, it's importantA. To use a dedicated email marketing serviceB. To integrate your efforts with social mediaC. To send resulting traffic to a dedicated landing page
quizSrc.definition: A. To use a dedicated email marketing service

quizSrc.term: What are the main reasons a hotel should work with OTA's?A. Billoard EffectB. ReachC. Pay-per-performanceD. ReactivityE. Market Information
quizSrc.definition: A. Billoard Effect  B. Reach  C. Pay-per-performance  D. Reactivity  E. Market Information

quizSrc.term: What does the Billboard Effect mean?A. Using an OTA also increases the number of direct bookings on a hotel websiteB. Agressive merchandising techniques can be used to create a sense of emergency to panic the customer into commiting the purchaseC. Working with OTAs allows hotels to save on the cost of building and updating a direct website
quizSrc.definition: A. Using an OTA also increases the number of direct bookings on a hotel website

quizSrc.term: Pay-per-Perfomance meansA. The hotel has to pay the OTA an initial set-up or periodic on-going feeB. The hotel only pays when the OTA is successful in driving a booking
quizSrc.definition: B. The hotel only pays when the OTA is successful in driving a booking

quizSrc.term: What can you do to increase direct bookings in spite of price parity?A. Use loyalty programs as an incentiveB. Translate your website in as many foreign languages as possibleC. Provide added value for the same rate on your brand.com websiteD. Upsell packages including spa treatments, wifi access or tickets to local attractions
quizSrc.definition: A. Use loyalty programs as an incentive  C. Provide added value for the same rate on your brand.com website  D. Upsell packages including spa treatments, wifi access or tickets to local attractions

quizSrc.term: When working with an OTA, what are the key success factors for maximising business?A. Availability ManagementB. PhotosC. User reviewsD. Competitive ratesE. Content
quizSrc.definition: A. Availability Management  B. Photos  C. User reviews  D. Competitive rates  E. Content

quizSrc.term: Which information should a hotel stress in the textual content provided to the OTA?A. Its locationB. Description of hotel facilitiesC. The manager's name and career historyD. A list of the amenities provided in the guestroomE. A list of nearby competing hotelsF. Local attractions
quizSrc.definition: A. Its location  B. Description of hotel facilities  D. A list of the amenities provided in the guestroom  F. Local attractions

quizSrc.term: Insuring the product and service provided match customer expectations is a good way to ...A. help insure positive user reviewsB. maximise repeat business
quizSrc.definition: A. help insure positive user reviews

quizSrc.term: You should usually be open and available for sale on your selected OTA channels, because ...A. leaving rooms vacant when they could be sold by the OTA is a false economyB. you need to sell each and every room at the maximum possible price and minimum cost each and every nightC. OTAs are valuable partners and you need to develop a working relationship with them to maximise business with them in the long term
quizSrc.definition: A. leaving rooms vacant when they could be sold by the OTA is a false economy  B. you need to sell each and every room at the maximum possible price and minimum cost each and every night  C. OTAs are valuable partners and you need to develop a working relationship with them to maximise business with them in the long term

quizSrc.term: Analytics-based techniques in revenue management are used to help forecast consumer behavior at the hotel's market level so as to be able to optimize room sales per night at an optimum price.A. TrueB. False
A practical example of revenue management in action is tailoring your room pricing in advance to fit future events, impactful weekends or seasons.A. FalseB. True
Revenue management finds its roots in yield management pioneered by Robert Crandall for use in airlines.A. TrueB. False

In answer to deregulation and fierce competition, American Airlines developed yield management to include advance-purchase restriction, capacity control and non-refundable tickets. The result was that customers turned away from American Airlines causing a loss in profits for the company.A. FalseB. True

Crandall inspired Bill Marriott, CEO of Marriott International, to adopt and enhance yield management specifically for his hotel chain. Which of the following two methods did Marriott employ?A. Targeted discounts based on demandB. Forecasting booking patterns and optimizing room availability by price and length of stay.C. Using intermediaries to handle Marriott bookings
quizSrc.definition: A. Targeted discounts based on demand   B. Forecasting booking patterns and optimizing room availability by price and length of stay.

quizSrc.term: Traditionally, travelers booked directly with "stay brands", meaning hotels that competed with each other to attract guests. Now, the "booking brand" has become the dominant point of entry for consumersA. TrueB. False
A hotel's marketing costs tend to rise as they both pay to obtain traffic from "booking brands" while at the same time competing with "stay brands".A. FalseB. True

Why is rate parity for bookings important for a hotel? (Please tick ALL that apply)A. If a hotel has a higher price on its own brand website, the customer will be tempted to book through a third-party meaning that the hotel will have to pay a commissionB. Price parity is important because potential foreign guests will be confused by any differenceC. If a hotel has a lower price on its own brand website, it will run the risk of breaching the rules of price parity clauses in their OTA contractsD. It isn't important because the priority is maximizing profit at any cost
quizSrc.definition: A. If a hotel has a higher price on its own brand website, the customer will be tempted to book through a third-party meaning that the hotel will have to pay a commission  C. If a hotel has a lower price on its own brand website, it will run the risk of breaching the rules of price parity clauses in their OTA contracts

quizSrc.term: Hotels are spending about 20%-30% of room revenue for customer acquisition before the customer even walks through the door. Which of the following isn't included in the calculations of these costs?A. TaxesB. Transaction feesC. CommissionsD. Sales and marketing costs
Individual hotels or small chains competing with each other to offer the lowest prices also often end up paying the highest commissions for those bookings.A. TrueB. False
PPTC means:A. Product, Price, Time, CustomerB. Product, Place, Time, CustomerC. Positioning, Price, Terms, Contract
Traditionally in the hotel marketplace two types of segmentation come to mind: yield/pricing segmentation and type of hotel segmentationA. FalseB. True

Hotels typically start with four macro-level segments: transient, corporate, group and other. This segmentation can then be customized based on the location and other characteristics of the property.A. FalseB. True

Hotels have looked to ______________ for inspiration in order to understand how to set up their online booking engine to offer special rates once a customer logs in based on that individual customer's worth (per-customer stay and spend) to the hotel.A. Leisure parksB. CasinosC. Airlines
Constrained forecasting measures demand controlled by hotel capacity, which is the number of rooms that you have available in your hotel. It is used for:A. PricingB. Financial purposes
What word is given to when demand outpaces supply for a given day for a given hotel?A. TransgressionB. CompressionC. Depression

From a revenue manager's perspective, if you're able to forecast accurately you can then price effectively and optimize revenue. But what mistake should revenue managers avoid?A. Price to budgetB. Set pricing to forecastsC. Set budgeting to seasonal data
Initially hotels offered the same room and room types for the same prices every day of the year. This was called:A. BARB. SeasonalC. Single-rate pricing
Which concept of pricing goes back to the business vs. leisure traveler split?A. BAR-LOSB. Weekday/WeekendC. Single-rate pricing
Which of the following offers a "semi-dynamic" pricing solution?A. BAR by LOSB. BAR
A hotel's "______________" is the rate at which it is obtaining bookingsA. pick-upB. pace
A hotel's "______________" is amount of bookings over a certain time intervalA. pick-upB. pace

What should the revenue manager do if he/she starts to notice a specific customer segment beginning to have a higher volume of pick-up than they had forecast over a certain period of time?A. Offer discountsB. Raise pricesC. Decrease prices

Effective yielding is a hotel's solution to optimize their revenues against their increasing costs. To maximize revenues over both high demand periods and need periods, what can be done?A. Shut down discount offersB. Increase internet presenceC. Independently price every segment

What would result if you closed out your discount offer?A. OTAs would no longer show your property on their listsB. A prospective high paying or long staying customer may not find you because he or she searched for that discount and it would show no availabilityC. Demand would rise because your hotel would be seen as selective
quizSrc.definition: B. A prospective high paying or long staying customer may not find you because he or she searched for that discount and it would show no availability

quizSrc.term: Open pricing enables you to leave discounts open during high demand periods, and lower the discount to capitalize on the demand.A. FalseB. True

One of the most important things for a revenue manager to understand is how critical price and time are, and the sensitivity of both, because these allow you to really understand the customer and the consumer's behavior.A. falseB. True

"The essence of revenue management analytics is in understanding consumers' perception of product __________________________, and accurately aligning product____________, __________________and ___________________ within each customer segment." Which of the following words does not belong to the statement?A. PricesB. ValueC. Life-cycleD. AvailabilityE. Placement
If you have multiple customers with different pricing characteristics in the same segment, you're missing revenue.A. FalseB. True
There are two major types of segmentation: one for pricing and the other for marketing purposes.A. FalseB. True

What is the goal with segmentation? Which statement is not true?A. Show an understanding of how you bucket together customer types to enable you then use these core groups to obtain more detailed segmentation.B. Categories of customers should not be drawn up depending on which actions you want to take but rather on which financial objectives you wish to achieve. (right answer)C. Different types of segmentation can be utilized as levers to control consumer actions - primarily purchasing or not purchasing a room at the hotel.
quizSrc.definition: B. Categories of customers should not be drawn up depending on which actions you want to take but rather on which financial objectives you wish to achieve. (right answer)

quizSrc.term: The rise in Booking brands does not necessarily mean the end of Stay brands. Each has their strong point. Which of the following three words best define their respective strengths?A. Producing customer loyaltyB. Being a central point of informationC. producing customer experiencesD. MarketingE. Providing customer delight
quizSrc.definition: B. Being a central point of information  C. producing customer experiences  D. Marketing

quizSrc.term: The cost of acquisition is one of the most important aspects of distribution, revenue management and segmentation. Understanding your costs enables you to:A. Maximize the rate that you can charge and maximize your segmentationB. Minimize the rate that you can charge and minimize marketing costsC. Optimize the rate that you can charge and optimize your distribution strategy
quizSrc.definition: C. Optimize the rate that you can charge and optimize your distribution strategy

quizSrc.term: The increase in complexity of the distribution landscape has two consequences for segmentation: Complications and Power.A. FalseB. True

Hotels typically use two major types of segmentation: there's the yielding segmentation that is geared towards pricing and then there is market segmentation that is more geared toward financial reporting.A. TrueB. False

As a rule of thumb if there is a segment that consistently generates between _________ of your room nights or revenue, it makes sense for a hotel to separate it into its own segment.A. 8-15%B. 15-20%C. 1-5%

To reach optimal segmentation, there are:A. 3 key considerations to take into accountB. 4 key considerations to take into accountC. 2 key considerations to take into accountD. 5 key considerations to take into account
quizSrc.definition: B. 4 key considerations to take into account

quizSrc.term: A distribution channel is simply a channel to get people to hotels and may include hotel websites, online travel agencies, and wholesalers. Which two factors are important to cover?A. Transport and infrastructure in the immediate area of your propertyB. Evaluate your needs as a property - which distribution channels fill your property bestC. Develop a strategy both for the present, short term and long term future
quizSrc.definition: B. Evaluate your needs as a property - which distribution channels fill your property best   C. Develop a strategy both for the present, short term and long term future

quizSrc.term: A hotel can get huge exposure to consumers through online travel agencies and therefore they are a valuable player in the distribution value chain. What is key from the operational perspective?A. Selecting your OTA based on the lowest commission per first stayB. Converting a customer into a routine or loyal guest after that first stay purchased through an OTAC. Deciding which guests will most probably not return to the property in the future
quizSrc.definition: B. Converting a customer into a routine or loyal guest after that first stay purchased through an OTA

quizSrc.term: What is important when comparing price and behavior?A. Maintaining prices that are different to market or consumer behaviorB. Maintaining brand imageC. Maintaining one price for all customer and market behaviors
quizSrc.definition: A. Maintaining prices that are different to market or consumer behavior   B. Maintaining brand image

quizSrc.term: Hotels can't entirely predict market behavior so they need to anticipate some prices, but they can't just set prices without anticipating market behavior. Some customers will only buy on a good deal and others don't care and will buy regardless of price. Analyzing how consumers come to channels, and their spend patterns, is a good way of determining this. Is this statement:A. FalseB. True

There are three major questions to take into account when thinking about re-segmentation: 1) What type of business or mix of business does the hotel have? 2) Can you tell the booking age of each segment of customer, ADR, booking lead time? 3) Are your revenue and sales and marketing teams pricing and promotional strategies resulting in the hotel selling out the day of the stay?A. TrueB. False

There are three key questions a hotel should ask itself to determine if they need to re-segment. Which one of the following isn't included in these key questions?A. If yes, are you selling out day-off?B. If yes, can you forecast what each business segment will bring to turnover and hotel profit?C. Can you tell the mix of business that it has? If not, refer back to the circle of segmentation optimization.D. If yes, can you tell the booking behavior of each customer segment, ADR and booking lead-time?
quizSrc.definition: B. If yes, can you forecast what each business segment will bring to turnover and hotel profit?

quizSrc.term: There are three major efforts a hotel can make in order to best manage the changes arising from third-party distribution and re-connect with all customer segments. The first of these is: __________________ to better identify and understand the different customer behaviors in the market place to optimize pricing.A. Optimize the IT systemB. Use a computerC. Utilize more data

There are three major efforts a hotel can make in order to best manage the changes arising from third-party distribution and re-connect with all the customer segments. The second of these is: Re-think segmentation ___________________to target consumers as dynamically as possible to optimize promotions.A. In a more detailed wayB. In a global wayC. According to hotel teams
quizSrc.definition: A. In a more detailed way

quizSrc.term: There are three major efforts a hotel can make in order to best manage the changes arising from third-party distribution and re-connect with all customer segments. The third of these is:_________________acquisition costs and other key metrics to optimize distribution.A. BenchmarkingB. StabilizingC. Integrating
In the context of revenue management, forecasting means anticipating a certain amount of demand around specific customer segments and, in aggregate, an entire hotel property.A. FalseB. True
There are two major means of forecasting: (1) unconstrained forecasts or those controlled by capacity and (2) constrained forecasts or those not controlled by capacity.A. TrueB. False
In terms of forecasting, variance is a comparison between two hotels in a typical hospitality year.A. FalseB. True

Forecast-to-budget variance gives you an indication of your forecasted performance (with current on the books production) versus what you budgeted and how far ahead or behind you are pacing.A. TrueB. False
When forecasting, compression is when supply exceeds demand and the result is a compressed market.A. FalseB. True

What does RevPAR show?A. The efficiency of the revenue compared to the number of customers who stay at the propertyB. The revenue generated per customer segmentC. The revolving rate of clients per price and per room
quizSrc.definition: A. The efficiency of the revenue compared to the number of customers who stay at the property

quizSrc.term: A property's constrained forecast is demand controlled by capacity.A. FalseB. True

Unconstrained forecast is total demand for the property if capacity is not a factor. In this instance, if a hotel sells its one hundred rooms, its unconstrained forecast would show the overall market demand for its property on a given night.A. FalseB. True

To track pace means:A. Monitoring the number of customers booking over a given period of timeB. Monitoring the place an actual booking occurs, i.e. online or at the front deskC. Monitoring the rapidity of hotel operations
quizSrc.definition: A. Monitoring the number of customers booking over a given period of time

quizSrc.term: Badly forecasting or under-forecasting is detrimental to a hotel because it may lead to the hotel dropping rates and taking last-minute bookings through discount channels and thus paying high commissions.A. TrueB. False

In terms of forecasting and the results achieved from this, what do operations, revenue managers, and others at the property generally use as a health benchmark for the property?A. InventoryB. DevelopmentC. PerformanceD. Staffing

Which of the following developing data points are being increasingly incorporated into the revenue management process?A. Customer genderB. Property-level booking dataC. Competitor pricingD. Customer nationalityE. Weather
quizSrc.definition: B. Property-level booking data  C. Competitor pricing  E. Weather

quizSrc.term: One of the most correlated data points is between unconstrained demand forecast and web site traffic.A. TrueB. False

Which two data points are factors to consider from a macro-level when forecasting a hotel?A. Monitoring competitor pricingB. Monitoring online presenceC. Monitoring the price of air travelD. Monitoring inflation
quizSrc.definition: A. Monitoring competitor pricing   B. Monitoring online presence

quizSrc.term: Pricing in a nutshell is the output after the application of segmentation and forecasting to current market conditions. A. True B. False
What is important when thinking about pricing and reservations coming in through various channels? A. The popularity of each channel B. The overall number of consumers C. The cost of each channel
quizSrc.definition: C. The cost of each channel

quizSrc.term: A pricing approach is the methodology around which you want to structure your pricing plan. The pricing strategy is the philosophy by which to execute the pricing plan. A. False B. True

Many hotels often don’t think from a strategic standpoint when offering pricing through promotional channels, offering better promotions on last minute discount platforms than through their own brand.com site. What negative effects does this generate? A. It will most likely drive potential customers to third-party distributors and generate a commission fee for the hotel B. It will turn away loyal customers to book directly from online third-party platforms and thereby decrease repeat business C. It will cause third-party booking agencies to then increase their prices
quizSrc.definition: A. It will most likely drive potential customers to third-party distributors and generate a commission fee for the hotel

quizSrc.term: Of the three pricing approaches, the budget-driven pricing approach is the least positive in that it: A. Removes the dynamism required to make pricing optimize revenue B. Means that the market and demand factors are overlooked C. Doesn’t include fixed costs like facilities and salaries
quizSrc.definition: A. Removes the dynamism required to make pricing optimize revenue B. Means that the market and demand factors are overlooked

quizSrc.term: Many hoteliers drive pricing by wanting to be priced off of a specific competitor. This is not the best methodology, as a hotel will find itself in a position of market _____________. A. Hindrance B. Leader C. Follower D. Trend-setter

A dynamic, data-driven pricing approach enables (select as most appropriate): A. Software to be standardized throughout the property or properties B. Help make accurate forecasts using micro and macro data sets C. Uses a variety of historical and forward-looking data to determine a price for a hotel D. Costs related to employee working hours in the pricing process to be reduced
quizSrc.definition: A. Software to be standardized throughout the property or properties B. Help make accurate forecasts using micro and macro data sets C. Uses a variety of historical and forward-looking data to determine a price for a hotel D. Costs related to employee working hours in the pricing process to be reduced

quizSrc.term: Hotels typically benchmark their rate using a metric called ______________ A. GDP B. ADR C. BDR D. GDR
If you are manually forecasting and determining a price there are ________ basic things to be considering to give guidelines to pricing decisions: A. 4 B. 3 C. 2

A hotel’s “pace” is the __________ at which they’re getting bookings, and then a hotel’s “pick up” is the __________ of bookings over a certain ___________. Which three words successfully complete the statement? A. Booking agency B. Rate C. Percentage D. Amount E. Time interval
quizSrc.definition: A. Booking agency B. Rate D. Amount E. Time interval

quizSrc.term: Of the following elements studied in Module 4, which ones are recommended to be used most? A. All of the above B. Market Volatility & Demand Reports C. Booking Curve Management: Pace & Pick Up D. Competitive Set Pricing
quizSrc.definition: A. All of the above B. Market Volatility & Demand Reports C. Booking Curve Management: Pace & Pick Up D. Competitive Set Pricing

quizSrc.term: There are 7 most common pricing mistakes. One of the following is an intruder! Which one? A. Selling Out Too Late B. Not Changing Rates C. Shutting Down Prices D. Linking Different Price Points E. Selling on First-Come Basis F. Using Gut Feeling G. Sudden Pricing Changes

With a fixed-tier BAR strategy, you set one price and everything derives from that and you’re done. Clearly the benefit of this methodology is its simplicity. But what is the major drawback with using this method? A. It increases the threat of breaking parity-rate clauses B. It dissuades potential customers from staying at your property C. It restricts rate availability to the customer
quizSrc.definition: C. It restricts rate availability to the customer

quizSrc.term: What are the key benefits of open-pricing? Select the three most appropriate from the following list. A. Allows for long-term forecasting of the booking curve B. Keeps all channels open thereby resulting in more exposure for a hotel C. Maximizes revenue during both peak and need periods D. Independently pricing every segment
quizSrc.definition: A. Allows for long-term forecasting of the booking curve B. Keeps all channels open thereby resulting in more exposure for a hotel C. Maximizes revenue during both peak and need periods D. Independently pricing every segment

quizSrc.term: Paradoxically, as for fixed-BAR, open-pricing aims to restrict rate availability. A. False B. True

One way the hotel industry has recently worked to regain direct bookings is through loyalty segmentation pricing. The idea is to: A. Increase loyalty by refusing to work with third-party online booking agencies B. Increase loyalty by providing additional value or better rates to your loyal and most profitable customers C. Increase loyalty by raising rates and therefore creating a “selective” need for the potential customer
quizSrc.definition: A. Increase loyalty by refusing to work with third-party online booking agencies B. Increase loyalty by providing additional value or better rates to your loyal and most profitable customers

quizSrc.term: What is a correct definition of pricing elasticity? A. A measure used in economics to show how much a price can be stretched higher to increase revenue B. A measure used in industry to measure the cost of raw materials in the making of elastics and other rubber-related products C. A measure used in economics to show the responsiveness, or elasticity, of the quantity demanded of a good or service to a change in its price
quizSrc.definition: C. A measure used in economics to show the responsiveness, or elasticity, of the quantity demanded of a good or service to a change in its price

quizSrc.term: The more complicated a hotel’s distribution and the more dynamic the pricing, the harder it is to actually get those rates in front of the consumer A. True B. False

Revenue strategy should deliver four main aspects: Incorporate cost levers, Evaluate and optimize performance, Make optimal decisions for resource allocations, and Deliver growing profits. The basis of a strong revenue strategy starts with revenue management. Which 3 elements are key to effective revenue management? A. Segmentation, Forecasting and budgeting, Data base management B. Segmentation, Forecasting and budgeting, Pricing C. Yield management, Customer Loyalty policy, Inventory management
quizSrc.definition: B. Segmentation, Forecasting and budgeting, Pricing

quizSrc.term: Analytics-based techniques in revenue management are used to help forecast consumer behavior at the hotel’s market level so as to be able to optimize room sales per night at an optimum price. A. False B. True
A practical example of revenue management in action is tailoring your room pricing in advance to fit future events, impactful weekends or seasons. A. True B. False
Revenue management finds its roots in yield management pioneered by Robert Crandall for use in airlines. A. False B. True

In answer to deregulation and fierce competition, American Airlines developed yield management to include advance-purchase restriction, capacity control and non-refundable tickets. The result was that customers turned away from American Airlines causing a loss in profits for the company. A. False B. True

Crandall inspired Bill Marriott, CEO of Marriott International, to adopt and enhance yield management specifically for his hotel chain. Which of the following two methods did Marriott employ? A. Forecasting booking patterns and optimizing room availability by price and length of stay. B. Using intermediaries to handle Marriott bookings C. Targeted discounts based on demand
quizSrc.definition: A. Forecasting booking patterns and optimizing room availability by price and length of stay. C. Targeted discounts based on demand

quizSrc.term: Traditionally, travelers booked directly with “stay brands”, meaning hotels that competed with each other to attract guests. Now, the “booking brand” has become the dominant point of entry for consumers A. True B. False
A hotel’s marketing costs tend to rise as they both pay to obtain traffic from “booking brands” while at the same time competing with “stay brands”. A. True B. False

Why is rate parity for bookings important for a hotel? (Please tick ALL that apply) A. Price parity is important because potential foreign guests will be confused by any difference B. It isn’t important because the priority is maximizing profit at any cost C. If a hotel has a higher price on its own brand website, the customer will be tempted to book through a third-party meaning that the hotel will have to pay a commission D. If a hotel has a lower price on its own brand website, it will run the risk of breaching the rules of price parity clauses in their OTA contracts
quizSrc.definition: A. Price parity is important because potential foreign guests will be confused by any difference C. If a hotel has a higher price on its own brand website, the customer will be tempted to book through a third-party meaning that the hotel will have to pay a commission D. If a hotel has a lower price on its own brand website, it will run the risk of breaching the rules of price parity clauses in their OTA contracts

quizSrc.term: Hotels are spending about 20%-30% of room revenue for customer acquisition before the customer even walks through the door. Which of the following isn’t included in the calculations of these costs? A. Sales and marketing costs B. Taxes C. Commissions D. Transaction fees
Individual hotels or small chains competing with each other to offer the lowest prices also often end up paying the highest commissions for those bookings. A. True B. False
PPTC means: A. Product, Price, Time, Customer B. Positioning, Price, Terms, Contract C. Product, Place, Time, Customer
Traditionally in the hotel marketplace two types of segmentation come to mind: yield/pricing segmentation and type of hotel segmentation A. False B. True

Hotels typically start with four macro-level segments: transient, corporate, group and other. This segmentation can then be customized based on the location and other characteristics of the property. A. False B. True

Hotels have looked to ______________ for inspiration in order to understand how to set up their online booking engine to offer special rates once a customer logs in based on that individual customer’s worth (per-customer stay and spend) to the hotel. A. Leisure parks B. Airlines C. Casinos
Constrained forecasting measures demand controlled by hotel capacity, which is the number of rooms that you have available in your hotel. It is used for: A. Financial purposes B. Pricing
What word is given to when demand outpaces supply for a given day for a given hotel? A. Depression B. Compression C. Transgression

From a revenue manager’s perspective, if you’re able to forecast accurately you can then price effectively and optimize revenue. But what mistake should revenue managers avoid? A. Set budgeting to seasonal data B. Set pricing to forecasts C. Price to budget
Initially hotels offered the same room and room types for the same prices every day of the year. This was called: A. Seasonal B. Single-rate pricing C. BAR
Which concept of pricing goes back to the business vs. leisure traveler split? A. Weekday/Weekend B. BAR-LOS C. Single-rate pricing
____________________enables each channel and segment to be independently priced based on the latent demand for each of those channels and segments. A. Independent Pricing B. Open Pricing C. BBLOS
A hotel’s “______________” is the rate at which it is obtaining bookings A. pace B. pick-up

What should the revenue manager do if he/she starts to notice a specific customer segment beginning to have a higher volume of pick-up than they had forecast over a certain period of time? A. Offer discounts B. Raise prices C. Decrease prices

Effective yielding is a hotel’s solution to optimize their revenues against their increasing costs. To maximize revenues over both high demand periods and need periods, what can be done? A. Shut down discount offers B. Increase internet presence C. Independently price every segment

What would result if you closed out your discount offer? A. OTAs would no longer show your property on their lists B. A prospective high paying or long staying customer may not find you because he or she searched for that discount and it would show no availability C. Demand would rise because your hotel would be seen as selective
quizSrc.definition: B. A prospective high paying or long staying customer may not find you because he or she searched for that discount and it would show no availability

quizSrc.term: Open pricing enables you to leave discounts open during high demand periods, and lower the discount to capitalize on the demand. A. True B. False

One of the most important things for a revenue manager to understand is how critical price and time are, and the sensitivity of both, because these allow you to really understand the customer and the consumer’s behavior. A. True B. false

The essence of revenue management analytics is in understanding consumers’ perception of product __________________________, and accurately aligning product____________, __________________and ___________________ within each customer segment.” Which of the following words does not belong to the statement? A. Life-cycle B. Value C. Availability D. Placement E. Prices
If you have multiple customers with different pricing characteristics in the same segment, you’re missing revenue. A. True B. False
There are two major types of segmentation: one for pricing and the other for marketing purposes. A. True B. False

What is the goal with segmentation? Which statement is not true? A. Categories of customers should not be drawn up depending on which actions you want to take but rather on which financial objectives you wish to achieve. (right answer) B. Different types of segmentation can be utilized as levers to control consumer actions – primarily purchasing or not purchasing a room at the hotel. C. Show an understanding of how you bucket together customer types to enable you then use these core groups to obtain more detailed segmentation.
quizSrc.definition: A. Categories of customers should not be drawn up depending on which actions you want to take but rather on which financial objectives you wish to achieve. (right answer)

quizSrc.term: The rise in Booking brands does not necessarily mean the end of Stay brands. Each has their strong point. Which of the following three words best define their respective strengths? A. Marketing B. Providing customer delight C. Being a central point of information D. producing customer experiences E. Producing customer loyalty
quizSrc.definition: A. Marketing B. Providing customer delight C. Being a central point of information

quizSrc.term: The cost of acquisition is one of the most important aspects of distribution, revenue management and segmentation. Understanding your costs enables you to: A. Minimize the rate that you can charge and minimize marketing costs B. Optimize the rate that you can charge and optimize your distribution strategy C. Maximize the rate that you can charge and maximize your segmentation
quizSrc.definition: B. Optimize the rate that you can charge and optimize your distribution strategy

quizSrc.term: The increase in complexity of the distribution landscape has two consequences for segmentation: Complications and Power. A. False B. True

Hotels typically use two major types of segmentation: there’s the yielding segmentation that is geared towards pricing and then there is market segmentation that is more geared toward financial reporting. A. True B. False

As a rule of thumb if there is a segment that consistently generates between _________ of your room nights or revenue, it makes sense for a hotel to separate it into its own segment. A. 8-15% B. 15-20% C. 1-5%

To reach optimal segmentation, there are: A. 5 key considerations to take into account B. 2 key considerations to take into account C. 4 key considerations to take into account D. 3 key considerations to take into account
quizSrc.definition: A. 5 key considerations to take into account

quizSrc.term: A distribution channel is simply a channel to get people to hotels and may include hotel websites, online travel agencies, and wholesalers. Which two factors are important to cover? A. Evaluate your needs as a property – which distribution channels fill your property best B. Develop a strategy both for the present, short term and long term future C. Transport and infrastructure in the immediate area of your property
quizSrc.definition: A. Evaluate your needs as a property – which distribution channels fill your property best B. Develop a strategy both for the present, short term and long term future

quizSrc.term: A hotel can get huge exposure to consumers through online travel agencies and therefore they are a valuable player in the distribution value chain. What is key from the operational perspective? A. Converting a customer into a routine or loyal guest after that first stay purchased through an OTA B. return to the property in the future C. Selecting your OTA based on the lowest commission per first stay
quizSrc.definition: A. Converting a customer into a routine or loyal guest after that first stay purchased through an OTA

quizSrc.term: What is important when comparing price and behavior? A. Maintaining one price for all customer and market behaviors B. Maintaining prices that are different to market or consumer behavior C. Maintaining brand image
quizSrc.definition: A. Maintaining one price for all customer and market behaviors B. Maintaining prices that are different to market or consumer behavior C. Maintaining brand image

quizSrc.term: Hotels can’t entirely predict market behavior so they need to anticipate some prices, but they can’t just set prices without anticipating market behavior. Some customers will only buy on a good deal and others don’t care and will buy regardless of price. Analyzing how consumers come to channels, and their spend patterns, is a good way of determining this. Is this statement: A. True B. False

There are three major questions to take into account when thinking about re-segmentation: 1) What type of business or mix of business does the hotel have? 2) Can you tell the booking age of each segment of customer, ADR, booking lead time? 3) Are your revenue and sales and marketing teams pricing and promotional strategies resulting in the hotel selling out the day of the stay? A. True B. False

There are three key questions a hotel should ask itself to determine if they need to re-segment. Which one of the following isn’t included in these key questions? A. If yes, are you selling out day-off? B. Can you tell the mix of business that it has? If not, refer back to the circle of segmentation optimization. C. If yes, can you tell the booking behavior of each customer segment, ADR and booking lead-time? D. If yes, can you forecast what each business segment will bring to turnover and hotel profit?
quizSrc.definition: D. If yes, can you forecast what each business segment will bring to turnover and hotel profit?

quizSrc.term: There are three major efforts a hotel can make in order to best manage the changes arising from third-party distribution and re-connect with all customer segments. The third of these is:_________________acquisition costs and other key metrics to optimize distribution. A. Integrating B. Benchmarking C. Stabilizing
In the context of revenue management, forecasting means anticipating a certain amount of demand around specific customer segments and, in aggregate, an entire hotel property. A. False B. True
There are two major means of forecasting: (1) unconstrained forecasts or those controlled by capacity and (2) constrained forecasts or those not controlled by capacity. A. True B. False
In terms of forecasting, variance is a comparison between two hotels in a typical hospitality year. A. True B. False

Forecast-to-budget variance gives you an indication of your forecasted performance (with current on the books production) versus what you budgeted and how far ahead or behind you are pacing. A. False B. True
When forecasting, compression is when supply exceeds demand and the result is a compressed market. A. True B. False

What does RevPAR show? A. The revenue generated per customer segment B. The efficiency of the revenue compared to the number of customers who stay at the property C. The revolving rate of clients per price and per room
quizSrc.definition: B. The efficiency of the revenue compared to the number of customers who stay at the property

quizSrc.term: A property’s constrained forecast is demand controlled by capacity. A. False B. True

Unconstrained forecast is total demand for the property if capacity is not a factor. In this instance, if a hotel sells its one hundred rooms, its unconstrained forecast would show the overall market demand for its property on a given night. A. True B. False

To track pace means: A. Monitoring the rapidity of hotel operations B. Monitoring the place an actual booking occurs, i.e. online or at the front desk C. Monitoring the number of customers booking over a given period of time
quizSrc.definition: C. Monitoring the number of customers booking over a given period of time

quizSrc.term: Badly forecasting or under-forecasting is detrimental to a hotel because it may lead to the hotel dropping rates and taking last-minute bookings through discount channels and thus paying high commissions. A. False B. True

In terms of forecasting and the results achieved from this, what do operations, revenue managers, and others at the property generally use as a health benchmark for the property? A. Inventory B. Development C. Staffing D. Performance

Which of the following developing data points are being increasingly incorporated into the revenue management process? A. Customer gender B. Customer nationality C. Property-level booking data D. Weather E. Competitor pricing
quizSrc.definition: A. Customer gender B. Customer nationality C. Property-level booking data D. Weather E. Competitor pricing

quizSrc.term: One of the most correlated data points is between unconstrained demand forecast and web site traffic. A. True B. False

Which two data points are factors to consider from a macro-level when forecasting a hotel? A. Monitoring competitor pricing B. Monitoring the price of air travel C. Monitoring online presence D. Monitoring inflation
quizSrc.definition: A. Monitoring competitor pricing B. Monitoring the price of air travel D. Monitoring inflation

quizSrc.term: Monitoring social review data carries with it a limitation: it can’t be tied to a specific customer segment so it is hard to have conclusive evidence of correlation with profita or forecasta. A. False B. True
Like competitor pricing data and review data, air traffic and weather can’t be tied directly to a specific customer segment. A. True B. False

Consumers typically book a hotel after they book air travel. What does this mean for hotels? A. It enables hotels to have insight into future increases or decreases in demand B. It enables hotels to contact the airlines and push sales with their offers
quizSrc.definition: A. It enables hotels to have insight into future increases or decreases in demand

quizSrc.term: Although Excel has traditionally been a lower-cost investment that could be managed in-house, it has its limitations. Select the most appropriate from the following. A. Latest technological advances are not continuously available as you have to wait until newer versions are developed and then distributed. B. A license has be purchased from the software provider C. The increasing complexity of data requires more powerful analytical engines D. In many cases, access to Excel spreadsheet is limited unless you are sitting at your computer
quizSrc.definition: D. In many cases, access to Excel spreadsheet is limited unless you are sitting at your computer

quizSrc.term: A key aspect of modern revenue strategy systems is they are built in true multi-tenant cloud architectures, allowing users to always use the most up-to-date version of the system.. A. False B. True

There are four major means or statistics to analyse your forecast accuracy. There are 3 of them included in the statements below: A. Simple error B. Mean absolute per cent error C. Complex error D. Simple per cent error
quizSrc.definition: A. Simple error B. Mean absolute per cent error D. Simple per cent error

quizSrc.term: Simple error often results in inflated forecast accuracy due to offsetting over- and under-forecasting. A. True B. False
Your mean absolute deviation or MAD is defined as a means of calculating forecast accuracy by the absolute sum of your successes. A. True B. False
Budgeting helps a hotel _____________ costs around strategies to execute forecasting. A. Control B. Input C. Delete

Which of the following statements is true? A. Understanding what the pulse is of your city enables you to understand how to plan for your budget B. The budgeting process is the same no matter what type of hotel you manage. C. Daily budgeting is not connected to the performance of your property
quizSrc.definition: A. Understanding what the pulse is of your city enables you to understand how to plan for your budget

quizSrc.term: For Economy Hotels simple forecasting using minimal segmentation is the expectation A. False B. True

Monitoring Pick-Up A 600-room hotel on the stay-date of December 30 has OTB numbers, for the entire property, shown below: Date Property OTB October 19 20 October 29 411 Based on this 10-day pick-up, should the property yield up, lower, or keep the rates the same for the yieldable rates? A. Lower Rates B. Keep the rates the same C. Yield Rates Up

Monitoring Pace A 150-room hotel has demand numbers for the stay date of November 1, for the entire property, shown below: Date Demand September 14 Unconstrained Demand over 100 % September 21 Unconstrained Demand over 100 % Based on this Week-over-Week variance in demand, should the property yield up, lower or keep the rates the same for the yieldable rates? A. Yield Rates Up B. Lower Rates C. Keep Rates the same

Conversion Rate A 225-room hotel has property-direct Internet booking engine conversation for the stay of December 14, for the entire property, shown below: Conversion Rate Normal 5% Current 15% Based on this conversion rate, should you yield up, lower, or keep the rates the same for rates on your booking engine? A. Yield Rates Up B. Lower Rates C. Keep Rates the same

Group A 200-room hotel has group OTB numbers for the stay date of December 15, for group OTB, shown below, the property lost a wedding group: Date Group OTB August 15 50 August 22 10 Based on losing this large group block should you yield up, lower, or keep the rates the same for your yieldable rates? A. Yield Rates Up B. Lower Rates C. Keep Rates the same

LRA increase A 250-room hotel has corporate LRA OTB numbers for the stay date of December 21, for the entire property, shown below: Date Corporate LRA OTB August 7 20 August 14 150 Based on this large 7-day pick-up should you yield up, lower or keep the rates the same (and implement restrictions) for your corporate rates? A. Keep Rates the same B. Lower Rates C. Yield Rates Up

Monitoring Pace & Reputation A 150-room hotel has demand numbers for the stay date of November 1, for the entire property, shown below. Additionally the property has been ranked above the comp set on online review scores. Date Demand September 14 Unconstrained demand over 100% September 21 Unconstrained demand over 100% Based on this Week-over-Week variance in demand should the property yield up, lower, or keep the rates the same for the yieldable rates? A. Lower Rates B. Yield Rates Up C. Keep Rates the same

Transient A 200-room hotel has group OTB numbers for the stay date of December 15, for the transient segment, shown below. Note: the property is pacing to sell out and transient pick-up is average. Date Transient OTB August 15 75 August 22 90 Based on this data, should you yield-up, lower or keep the rates the same for your transient rates? A. Yield Rates Up B. Keep Rates the same C. Lower Rates

OTA A 225-room hotel has group OTB numbers for the stay date of December 22, for the OTA OTB, shown below. Note: the property is pacing to sell out and OTA pick-up is high. Date OTA OTB July 15 75 July 22 150 Based on this data should you yield up, lower or keep the rates the same for your OTA rates? A. Yield Rates Up B. Lower Rates C. Keep Rates the same

Corporate nLRA A 400-room hotel has a corporate nLRA OTB for the stay date of December 30, for the corporate OTB, shown below. Note: the hotel is forecasted to sell-out. Date nLRA OTB September 10 20 September 17 150 Based on this data, knowing you cannot yield rates, should you put a length-of-stay restriction on the corporate segment? A. Yes B. No

Unexpected Group A 200-room hotel has group OTB numbers for the stay date of December 15, for group OTB, shown below; note this was not an expected group: Date Group OTB August 15 10 August 22 70 Based on losing this group pick-up, should you yield up, lower, or keep rates the same for you yieldable rates? A. Keep Rates the same B. Lower Rates C. Yield Up Rates

Expected Group A 200-room hotel has group OTB numbers for the stay date of March 15, for group OTB, shown below; note this was an expected group (meaning you forecasted the other segments knowing this group was coming): Date Group OTB January 2 10 January 16 50 Based on losing this group pick-up should you yield up, lower, or keep rates the same for your yieldable rates? A. Lower Rates B. Keep Rates the same C. Yield Up Rates

Cost Per Occupied Room On October 15, a 300-room hotel has a current price of $59 on their website for the stay date of November 22. Their cost per occupied room (or cleaning cost of the room) is $59. Based on this information, should the hotel consider lowering rates? A. Yes B. No

Monitoring demand A 150-room hotel has demand numbers for the stay date of November 1, for the entire property, shown below: Date Demand September 14 Unconstrained Demand over 100% September 21 Unconstrained Demand = 100% Based on this Week-over-Week variance in demand, should the property yield up, lower, or keep the rates the same for the yieldable rates? A. Keep Rates the same B. Yield Up Rates C. Lower Rates

Monitoring Demand A 200-room hotel has demand numers for the stay date of November 15, for the entire property, shown below: Date Demand September 23 Unconstrained Demand over 100% September 30 Unconstrained Demand = 90% Based on this Week-over-Week variance in demand, should the property yield up, lower, or keep the rates the same for the yieldable rates? A. Lower Rates B. Keep Rates the same C. Yield Up Rates

Monitoring Comp. Set Pricing & Demand On October 19, a 300-room hotel has an unconstrained demand of 90% for the stay date of December 20. All the other competitors in the market are lowering their rates. Based on this information, should the hotel raise or lower rates? A. Keep Rates the same B. Yield Rates Up C. Lower Rates
The net contribution approach compares: A. the spend versus the net revenue B. the revenue and the total costs of marketing
quizSrc.definition: A. the spend versus the net revenue

quizSrc.term: Advertising agency fees, reservation costs of the hotel’s booking engine or other IT, cost of creating the hotel’s website, cost of the personnel involved with the hotel’s direct marketing work are all: A. Ancillary costs B. Unnecessary costs that should be avoided
All the fees can be categorized and assigned to the correct channel. A. False B. True
When working with an Agency, you should request that they set up a proper attribution model and work with them to optimize the ad-spend based on the data. A. True B. False

Complete this statement: "The four pillars of marketing are…" A. Popularize, Capture, Convert and Share B. Dream, Search, Book, Experience C. Comfort, Location, Value, Price D. Promotion, Price, Place and Product
quizSrc.definition: A. Popularize, Capture, Convert and Share

quizSrc.term: Which is the most efficient way of popularizing a hotel? A. Banner ads B. Distribution channels (OTAs) C. Search Ads D. Word of Mouth
What is the next step once a hotel is popularized? A. Capture B. Promote C. Convert D. Share

What are the most important keywords and position for hotels to protect (or bid on) when considering digital marketing campaigns? A. the city's name listing B. the country's name listing C. the hotels name and listing D. the nearest monument name and listing
quizSrc.definition: C. the hotels name and listing

quizSrc.term: When a visitor has landed on the hotel's website, or the hotel's page on a distribution channel, the goal is to to turn them into a paid guest. What is the best way to do this? A. Showing the surroundings and not the rates as that might scare them off. B. Showing all the information to everyone who visits the page so they can read everything. C. Showing food and beverage information and activities around the hotel but not the rooms and rates as it may reduce conversions. D. Showing only the relevant information and limiting additional information to those that really need it
quizSrc.definition: D. Showing only the relevant information and limiting additional information to those that really need it

quizSrc.term: How does a hotel determine its USP? A. Understanding what satisfied clients comment on as their perception of the main advantages of the hotel. B. Studying the designers and owners brief for the hotel and determining it based on features. C. Staying at the hotel and nearby hotels working out the benefits for the hotel. D. Seeing the hotel and working out the top benefits for guests based on the hotel's features
quizSrc.definition: A. Understanding what satisfied clients comment on as their perception of the main advantages of the hotel.

quizSrc.term: Complete the sentence: "The 3 elements that make up a hotel's USP are…" A. Location, Location, Location B. Reviews, Price, Availability C. Location, Comfort and Value D. Promotion, Room Cost, Staff vs Room ratio
quizSrc.definition: D. Promotion, Room Cost, Staff vs Room ratio

quizSrc.term: What is the best way of optimizing distribution? A. Increasing commissions to OTAs B. Working with an agency C. Having great quality content D. Giving cheaper price through distribution channels

How does a hotel determine which channel should be awarded the most investment? A. Optimizing the highest producing channels and increasing direct bookings B. Working mainly on direct revenue through website C. Understanding the cost of distribution per channel and optimizing accordingly D. Working on the lowest producing channels and optimizing those to increase revenue
quizSrc.definition: C. Understanding the cost of distribution per channel and optimizing accordingly

quizSrc.term: How can a hotel increase the number of guests sharing their opinions about the property and their experience? A. Exceed expectations and ensure guests are aware of any bonuse they got. B. Ask guests to leave reviews via email, cards in room and at the front desk. C. Request that guests share information about the hotel to enter a contest D. Arrange for freebies to all guests
quizSrc.definition: A. Exceed expectations and ensure guests are aware of any bonuse they got.
